passage:
Yamini, you asked about my favourite singer, so here goes. I’m Disha, and I was fifteen, and I’d played her album every night for two years. Last month a report said she had treated her staff badly for a long time and hidden it.
First I refused to read it. Then I read it and felt sick. I didn’t delete the songs, because a couple of them got me through exams. But I stopped posting her lyrics.
When my friends said, “People exaggerate,” I said, “The songs are still good, and what she did is still wrong.” Nobody answered. Holding both things feels strange, but pretending felt worse.

qa.q: How old was Disha when the album played every night?
qa.a: Disha was fifteen and had played the album every night for two years.

qa.q: What was Disha feeling after reading the report?
qa.a: Disha felt sick and deeply disappointed after reading it, which shows how much the singer had meant to Disha.

qa.q: What choice did Disha make about the songs, and why did it work?
qa.a: Disha kept the songs but stopped posting the lyrics. That kept what was good in the music without excusing what the singer did.

qa.q: What might Disha's friends who said people exaggerate have been feeling?
qa.a: They may have been trying to protect their own admiration, or avoiding the discomfort of the report. Their silence after Disha's answer suggests they had no ready reply.

grounding: Shows a teenager working through disappointment in an admired singer, keeping the music without excusing the wrongdoing.

passage:
Kishore had a poster of an actor above his desk. When news broke that the actor had shouted at junior crew members and then apologised in a half-hearted way, Kishore stared at the poster for a long time. I’m Karthik, his classmate, and I was next to him.
Manoj said, “So what? Everyone does that.” Kishore said, “Not everyone.” Ayesha stayed silent and looked at her notebook.
That evening Kishore said, “I still like the films. What he did to those people isn’t okay, and I’m not going to pretend it is.” He took the poster down and slid it inside his cupboard door. I couldn’t tell whether he felt sad or angry.

qa.q: What did the actor do that upset Kishore?
qa.a: The actor shouted at junior crew members and then apologised in a half-hearted way.

qa.q: What might Kishore have been feeling as he stared at the poster?
qa.a: Kishore was probably disappointed, since the actor had been someone he admired. Karthik could not tell if it was sadness or anger, so both are possible.

qa.q: Which choice of Kishore's showed he could keep the good and still be honest?
qa.a: He said he still liked the films but refused to pretend the behaviour was fine. He then took the poster down rather than arguing about it.

qa.q: How might Ayesha, who stayed silent, have seen the exchange between Manoj and Kishore?
qa.a: Ayesha may have agreed with Kishore but felt it was hard to speak against Manoj, or she may have been unsure. Looking at her notebook shows she stayed out of it.

grounding: Shows a teenager, seen by a classmate, working through disappointment in an admired actor without excusing the behaviour.
